items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: I met Jolly Roll Morton the first time... I was introduced to Jolly Roll by Rhys Dupree... we nodded to each other as strangers... I began to make regular trips from Philadelphia to Washington, bringing people with me to see him then, and listen to him talk and play the piano.

ctx.x: So, what about, uh, Jolly Roll Morton? I'm skipping about. Excuse me.

All right. Mm-hmm. Well, I met Jolly Roll Morton the first time, uh, now, let's see, that's gotta be in nineteen thirty-seven, and, or maybe thirty-eight. I don't know, but it was in the winter at that time. Mm-hmm. I was introduced to Jolly Roll by Rhys Dupree, who, uh, claimed to have been, and may well have been, the composer of Shorten and Bread and Dupree Blues. And it was in a, in a hotel called the Douglas Hotel on Broad and Lombard Street in Philadelphia. I had seen Jolly Roll at the Lincoln Theater…
The first time you heard him there was when you were with Reece Dupree?
